## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A five-juan recension of the *Wùzhēn piān* 悟真篇 — Zhāng Bóduān's 張伯端 (984–1082) foundational *nèidān* poetic treatise of 1075, the second cornerstone of Chinese inner alchemy after the *Zhōuyì cāntóng qì* 周易參同契. Preserved as juan 26–30 of the *Xiūzhēn shíshū* 修真十書 in the *Zhèngtǒng Dàozàng* 正統道藏 (DZ 263e / CT 263.26 = TC 2:816–817), 洞真部 方法類. The collection comprises the oldest surviving commentaries on the *Wùzhēn piān*: the 1161 commentary of Yè Wénshū 葉文叔 (Yè Shìbiǎo 葉士表) — the earliest known *Wùzhēn piān* commentary, framed in terms of the *dàyǎn* 大衍 numerical scheme of the *Xìcí* 繫辭 appendix — together with commentaries variously attributed to Wēng Bǎoguāng 翁葆光 (under the names *Xiāngchuān wēng* 湘川翁 and *Wúmíng zǐ* 無名子) or Xuē Dàoguāng 薛道光. The whole was edited and brought together in 1202 by Yuán Gōngfǔ 遠公輔 (so the catalog meta; commonly written 袁公輔). The text was originally listed in *Zhízhāi shūlù jiětí* 直齋書錄解題 12.349 with the full title *Wùzhēn piān jízhù* 悟真篇集注. The present recension is the most complete surviving edition of the *Wùzhēn piān* itself: it preserves Zhāng Bóduān's eighty-one verses (sixteen *qīlǜ* 七律, sixty-four *jīnxī* keyed to the hexagrams, one closing on Tàiyī 太一), the twelve *Xījiāng yuè* 西江月 *cí*-lyrics, and the thirty-two Buddhist-themed poems (the *Chánzōng gēsòng* 禪宗歌頌; juan 30.1a–12a), the last of which are missing in the parallel recensions *[DZ 141 Wùzhēn piān zhùshū](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0141)* and *[DZ 142 Wùzhēn piān sānzhù](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0142)*. Five additional poems and a set of *Dānfáng bǎojiàn tú* 丹房寶鑑圖 diagrams (no author given) are appended.

**Abstract**

Farzeen Baldrian-Hussein, in Schipper & Verellen eds., *The Taoist Canon* (2004) 2:816–817 (§3.A.4.c, the *Wùzhēn piān* and the Southern School), describes the recensional history. The *Wùzhēn piān* was first listed in *Jùnzhāi dúshū zhì* 郡齋讀書志 (VDL 118) under the title *Tōngxuán bìyào Wùzhēn piān* 通玄祕要悟真篇 in one juan; quoted already in *[DZ 1017 Dàoshū](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c1017)* 18.9b by Zēng Zào 曾慥 (d. 1155), in *[Sāndòng qúnxiān lù](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d1248)* 2.9b (1154 preface), and in *[Dàodé zhēnjīng zhíjiě](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0688)* 2.12a (1159 preface). The first commentary by Yè Wénshū was completed in 1161; the present compilation by Yuán Gōngfǔ followed in 1202; and Wēng Bǎoguāng's commentary was already in circulation by 1173 (preface to *[Wùzhēn piān zhùshū](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0141)*). On the disputed authorship of the second commentary (Wēng Bǎoguāng vs. Xuē Dàoguāng) see Schipper-Verellen 2:818–823 and the apparatus at [KR5d0141](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0141); on the orderly arrangement of the poems, the present *Xiūzhēn shíshū* recension follows Zhāng Bóduān's stated programme more closely than any other Daozang witness. Frontmatter brackets composition between Zhāng's autograph preface of 1075 and Yuán Gōngfǔ's 1202 compilation.
